articles.title: Why Two Tabs Silently Overwrote Each Other: Field Notes on Lost Updates, Version Columns, and ETags
articles.excerpt: Headline: A lost update happens when two clients read the same record, both edit it, and the second save silently overwrites the first. Database transactions do not prevent it when the read and the wr…
articles.body: Headline: A lost update happens when two clients read the same record, both edit it, and the second save silently overwrites the first. Database transactions do not prevent it when the read and the write happen in separate HTTP requests; optimistic concurrency control does — an integer version column checked in the UPDATE 's WHERE clause, exposed to HTTP clients as an ETag and If-Match header, and shown to the user as an explicit conflict instead of silent data loss. I found this one while testing an admin panel I built. I opened the same product in two browser tabs, changed the price in one and saved, then changed the description in the other and saved. The price change was gone — no error, no failed request, no log line.
articles.author: Ahmed Mahmoud

articles.title: Octoverse 2026: AI Agents Now Write the First Draft of 40%+ of GitHub PRs
articles.excerpt: https://rohantechofficial.com/tech-news/github-octoverse-2026-ai-agent-pull-requests/ GitHub's Octoverse 2026, published October 28 at Universe, puts a number on what every developer has felt: agents…
articles.body: https://rohantechofficial.com/tech-news/github-octoverse-2026-ai-agent-pull-requests/ GitHub's Octoverse 2026, published October 28 at Universe, puts a number on what every developer has felt: agents are now a major source of code. By September 2026, more than 40% of pull requests started with a coding agent's first draft — up from 17% in March. That's 110 million agent-started PRs in a single month, about 6x March's volume. Definitions first: GitHub counts a PR as "agent-started" when its first draft came from an agent GitHub can detect. Detected use is a floor — the real number is higher. And it counts pull requests, not lines of code, so no, this doesn't mean 40% of all code is AI-written. The interesting part is velocity.

articles.title: Server-Driven Data Tables with Laravel, Inertia and React: Filters, Sorting and Pagination in the URL
articles.excerpt: Every business app eventually grows a table that people live in: products, invoices, suppliers, open orders. The first version is easy. Load everything, render a , maybe add a client-side filter. Then…
articles.body: Every business app eventually grows a table that people live in: products, invoices, suppliers, open orders. The first version is easy. Load everything, render a <table> , maybe add a client-side filter. Then the table hits 40,000 rows, someone asks for "sort by stock, only active items, page 3", and a colleague wants to send that exact view to a manager as a link. This post shows the pattern I use for server-driven data tables with Laravel, Inertia and React : the server does the filtering, sorting and pagination, and the browser URL is the single source of truth for the table's state. The problem with client-side tables Client-side tables break down in three predictable ways: Data size. Shipping every row to the browser works until it doesn't.

articles.excerpt: TL;DR A React PWA install prompt needs two paths. In Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet, catch beforeinstallprompt in a client component the root layout renders, call preventDefault, save the event and…
articles.body: TL;DR A React PWA install prompt needs two paths. In Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet, catch beforeinstallprompt in a client component the root layout renders, call preventDefault, save the event and call its prompt() from your own Install button; on iPhone and iPad no browser fires that event, so show the Share, then Add to Home Screen steps instead. Ask only after people get value, never inside the installed app, an in-app browser or a sign-up flow, and remember a Not now for a couple of weeks. A React PWA install prompt has to cover two kinds of browsers. Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet fire beforeinstallprompt , so your own button can open the browser's install dialog.

articles.title: Drupal AI: What the AI Modules Actually Do
articles.excerpt: Drupal AI has stopped being a scatter of provider-specific contributed modules that whoever needed them bolted on separately. It is now one coordinated project with an abstraction layer underneath it,…
articles.body: Drupal AI has stopped being a scatter of provider-specific contributed modules that whoever needed them bolted on separately. It is now one coordinated project with an abstraction layer underneath it, a security-team-covered release cycle, and a packaged product in Drupal CMS that offers to switch parts of it on during installation. The question worth asking has moved on from whether Drupal can do AI to which parts of it are worth turning on, and what each one costs once four editors use it every working day. Most write-ups stop at the demo. Somebody types a prompt, a page appears, a chatbot creates a content type while you watch. The demo is real.

articles.title: How a GPU Memory Mismatch Let Cloudflare's AI Serve One Customer Another's Data
articles.excerpt: https://rohantechofficial.com/tech-news/cloudflare-workers-ai-glm-data-leak/ Cloudflare's October 26 incident report is worth reading in full, because the bug is more interesting — and more instructiv…
articles.body: https://rohantechofficial.com/tech-news/cloudflare-workers-ai-glm-data-leak/ Cloudflare's October 26 incident report is worth reading in full, because the bug is more interesting — and more instructive — than the headline. For about two weeks (Aug 27–Sep 9), 155 responses from the GLM-5.3 model on Workers AI contained fragments of other customers' requests. All 155 went to prompts longer than 681,280 tokens. Nobody hacked anything. Two things went wrong at once. First, the model advertised a ~1M-token context window, but the GPUs' KV cache pool only fit 681,280 tokens — SGLang computes that pool from leftover GPU memory at startup, and nothing checked it against the advertised length.

articles.title: India launches next-gen navigation satellite to orbit (video)
articles.excerpt: India launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite to orbit today (Oct. 30) atop a GSLV rocket. It was the fourth orbital launch from Indian soil so far this year.
articles.body: India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30). A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time). Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026. (Image credit: ISRO) NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System ( GPS ).

articles.body: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable . With this control, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple AI companies, instead of setting them individually. The shared "policy token" signal is proposed by Kevin Kelley, a technical lead for standards at Anthropic, as part of the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF). articles.title: 5 horror franchises that went to space... and one that absolutely should have but didn't
articles.excerpt: In space, no one can hear you scream, a bit like the empty theater screens that some horror franchise's final installments limp. But there are still some real gems among the space-based frightfests.
articles.body: In space, no one can hear you scream... not unlike in the empty theater screens that aging horror franchises play to when the lustre has gone and their final installments limp to the public. It is perhaps little wonder that some horror franchises go to space to die... or take long breaks, at least. In celebration of Halloween , we're running down some horror franchises that made the journey to the final frontier, resulting in films that range from the sublime and outrageously campy fun to just pure awful. Absent from the list are space horror movies that have space baked into their natural fabric. So no Event Horizon, no Alien, and no Critters 4 (they were aliens, so they just went back to space; that doesn't count). 1.
